title: Exec sync — friction points & asks (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose: quick prep for 11/13 exec staff sync. Goal: surface the operational frictions that need leadership decisions or prioritization, and leave the meeting with clear owners for 3 near-term unblockers.

Attendees (proposed): CEO, CTO, Head of Product (Hosted API), Head of Serving Runtime, Head of SRE, Head of CS, Aisha (facilitator) — call out if anyone should be added/removed.

Topline ask summary (one-liners to put on the top slide):
- Approve 3-month spend flex for burst capacity (Dedicated) to avoid repeat latency SLO breaches for top 5 customers.
- Greenlight a staffed up SRE + infra hiring bucket (2 ICs, 1 manager) for Q1 to reduce on-call overload.
- Prioritize a security audit for Private on-prem package (risk: enterprise pipeline stalls).

Friction areas to surface (each with clarifying datapoints + desired decision):
1) Recurring latency SLO breaches for large customers (Hosted API)
   - Data: 9/10 SLOs normal, but last 6 weeks 3 distinct incidents where p95 drifted 30–70ms over target; incidents correlated with large synchronous rerank workloads (customer X and Y).
   - Root cause hypothesis: inefficient batching settings + fallback routing to lower-throughput variants causing queueing.
   - Ask: temporary capacity burst buy (Dedicated pool) while infra implements smarter routing (estimated 4–6 weeks). Decision needed: approve one-month package now (est. $120k) or allow degraded SLAs.

2) Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) certification slowdown
   - Data: Two enterprise deals paused in legal/security review (Deal A, Deal B). Sales says security audit/attestation is the blocking artifact.
   - Risk: ~ $1.1M ARR pipeline at risk if we don't produce an audit plan.
   - Ask: greenlight external pen-test + compliance advisory (SOC2 addendum) and attach a project owner in product/security. Decision: yes/no to spend up to $70k and assign owner.

3) Model regression monitoring gaps (evals/quality)
   - Data: Recent model swap triggered a quality regression on a core prompt set for retail customers; incident caught by CS but not automatically flagged by eval pipeline.
   - Gap: Eval coverage for production prompt sets is incomplete; no automated regression-triggered rollbacks.
   - Ask: allocate 3 sprint-weeks of research-engineering time to integrate evals into rollout pipeline (and add a rollback policy). Decision: prioritize in next alpha sprint or postpone.

4) Billing / chargeback confusion for Dedicated customers
   - Data: Two support tickets this month where customers were unexpectedly billed for burst capacity; invoice wording unclear.
   - Ask: approve standardized invoice language + change to billing flow (opt-in explicit) and a comms note. Decision: adopt proposed language (link in artifacts) and retroactively credit affected invoices.

Proposed meeting agenda (25 minutes total — keep tight):
- 0:00–0:03 — Quick status + purpose (Aisha)
- 0:03–0:10 — Latency incidents + capacity ask (Head of Serving Runtime) (decision: approve burst?)
- 0:10–0:15 — Private deployment audit ask (Head of Product + Head Security)
- 0:15–0:18 — Model regression monitoring ask (Applied ML lead)
- 0:18–0:22 — Billing invoice language + credits (Finance lead)
- 0:22–0:25 — Wrap, owners, near-term commits (Aisha)

Pre-reads (short) — please review before the meeting:
- Incident timeline doc: linked_artifacts / CONFTASK-4821 (short TL;DR in slide deck).
- Proposed burst capacity pricing and one-month estimate (internal sheet) — slack: #finance-proj (pinned).
- Draft invoice language (finance PR) — github link above.

Quick notes / temp analysis (for talking points):
- If exec approves burst, immediate action: finance signs PO, infra ramps new nodes into Dedicated pool (T+48 hrs), update routing policy to prefer Dedicated for high-throughput cron/rerank workloads.
- We should push an interim comms to impacted customers: "we're proactively adding capacity while we harden routing; no action required from you" — CS can draft.
- On regression monitoring: minimum viable fix = run daily diff against production prompt set -> if regression > threshold auto-tag rollout for pause. More robust = automated rollback.

Open questions (need quick answers before meeting if possible):
- Can finance clear a one-month $120k burst without board notice? (Michael).
- Who is the product owner for Private deployment compliance (Sofia?) — need explicit assignment.
- Is there a legal hurdle to crediting past invoices retroactively (legal/finance)?

Action items (post-meeting tracker — populate owner/ETA live in the meeting):
- AI-1: Create PO for 1-month Dedicated burst (owner: Michael Chen, ETA: 48 hrs if approved).
- AI-2: Draft external pen-test scope and vendor shortlist (owner: Head Security / Sofia Martinez, ETA: 5 business days).
- AI-3: Emergency comms draft for impacted customers (owner: Head CS, ETA: 24 hrs).
- AI-4: Add a minimal regression check to rollout pipeline (owner: Applied ML lead / Daniel Okoye, ETA: 2 sprints).
- AI-5: Update invoice copy and propose credits for affected accounts (owner: Finance lead, ETA: next billing run).

Notes-to-self / facilitation tips:
- Keep the capacity ask binary and timeboxed (one-month). Avoid scope creep in the meeting.
- If board-level flag is required on finance, offer a parallel path: sign contract contingent on board review (but that delays ramp).
- Use customer impact stories briefly (one-liner) — humanizes the ask.

Draft one-slide talking points (3 bullets each):
- Capacity: "We saw X minutes of elevated latency affecting N customers; short-term burst avoids outages while routing fix ships — est. $120k, 30 days".
- Private compliance: "Two deals stalled; external audit will clear the path for these and similar deals — est. $70k".
- Regression: "Auto-eval gap led to regression; small integration effort prevents reoccurrence".

Backup data to have ready (if asked):
- p95 latency charts (last 90 days) by customer (link to dashboards).
- Cost breakdown for burst (unit price / region / expected utilization).
- Signed NDAs / legal redlines for Private (if customer asks).

Risks to call out quickly:
- Spending on burst without routing fix just delays root cause and could repeat (we must pair money + infra sprint).
- Pen-test timeline could slip depending on vendor availability (ask for 2 vendor options).
- Retro credits set precedent — keep one-off if possible.

Draft follow-up email template after meeting (short):
"Thanks all — capture: [decision bullets]. Owners: [AI list]. I’ll follow up with PO / vendor shortlist / comms drafts by EOD Thu. If anything in the notes below needs correction, flag in thread."

Misc scratch thoughts (don't read aloud):
- Consider small pilot for customer X to test new routing logic before broad rollout (low-risk).
- Could we add a billing toggle in Console to control burst opt-in per account? Product / Console ask later.

-- end of scratchpad --

(Capture: will convert into slide deck and summary email after exec decisions; assign owners live and then move to shared drive exec-ops tracker.)
